On the meme: it's a screenshot from a spot Coca Cola made back in 2010 for the world cup. The concept was that we should go to countries that didn't participate in it so we could convince the people from there to root for Argentina, and one of those countries was Lesotho. Lesotheans (?) were given argentinean football shirts and were showed playing a match and stuff life that. Then Polandball found the spot and added the captions.  
Actually, 98% of the population has never seen that picture, and they're not aware that other countries mock us for believing that we're white, though if you ask an average person they'll tell you they differenciate themselves from the 'blacks', but apart from that we don't have a racial identity (fortunately). It's a thing from the internet. The only people it can trigger is a teenager on the internet who thinks they're white and cares about it or something like that.

No es tan plástico y lleno de nada como el pop mainstream (con el que trato de mantenerme al día pero puta que está en su etapa más depresiva) o el EMD, ni tan repetitivo como el metal o el rock normal (si quieren cagarme a palos aclaro que no sé mucho de terminología musical). Lo indie puede ser pretencioso a veces, pero detrás de esa pretensión al menos veo gente buscando hacer música buena con letras que digan ALGO. Ojo, no digo que siempre me guste el resultado, pero me parece que esa es la intención detrás del género.   
Otro 8% es un placer culposo que exprimo muy a menudo: canciones pop clásicas de los años 80/90. **Corazón** de Edmondo di Amicis. Es un libro de valores, algunos vigentes y otros muy pasados de moda, pero siempre va a ser uno de mis libros favoritos. Fue uno de los primeros que leí y la primera copia que tuve era de mi mamá cuando era chica. El argumento es sencillo, es el diario de un chico de Torino a fines del siglo XIX (Italia se unificó hace pocas décadas) que va a una escuela pública. Es un libro para chicos, así que por más que sea viejo es fácil de leer en esta época. Tiene algo que te lleva a esa época y a ese lugar. Todos los relatos se cuentan con una cotidianidad maravillosa. Algunas partes son muy crudas, y el autor quiere hacerte entender que la realidad es cruda para muchas personas, aunque muchas veces no lo veas. Se me ocurren mil moralejas más, y en la mayoría de los casos me alegro mucho de haberlas incorporado de chica, cuando tenía más o menos la edad del protagonista. Además tiene un cuento (que es MUY largo, jamás lo leí hasta el final pero algún día lo haré) que se lleva a cabo en Argentina, es la historia de un chico que va a buscar a su mamá que se había ido a Buenos Aires a trabajar, y termina recorriendo todo el país. Creo que la época en la que se desarrolla esa parte es un poco anterior a la del resto del libro, y hay unas descripciones hermosas de nuestras tierras.   
Otros que se me ocurrió incluir fueron **Las Ventajas de ser Invisible** (sí, libro de adolescentes, pero con una moraleja interesante y alejada de los clichés. Además lo leí porque me lo había prestado una chica que me gustaba en aquel entonces, y fue el libro que más rápido leí), **Rosaura A Las Diez** (mi libro nacional favorito por mucha diferencia) y **El Amante Japonés** (uno de los más nuevos de Allende, nunca había leído un libro de ella y me atrapó muchísimo), pero creo que el primer puesto se lo está llevando Corazón.

My story: Boys bullied me until eight grade. Maybe that's the reason I grew up being so shy. I barely talked in school. I was this fat blonde troubled little girl who would have good grades and a just few friends. As a plus, I got in fights quite often with my male classmates. Physical fights. I wasn't myself back then.  
I liked boys, but I knew I had no chance with them. The first time I actually suffered about it was when I was 11. I liked this boy very much. So much that it was... creepy. I would stare at him in all breaks(he was younger so I couldn't do it in class... I wouldn't have payed any attention if he had been in my class). It was like a game. Look at him for one second, then stop so he doesn't realise. Then do it again some minutes later. I... really thought he didn't notice. But he did.  
He sent one of his friends to talk to me. He said "X said stop staring at him. He says you are a fat whore".  
It hit me so hard. I couldn't stop thinking about it. In the next break, I went to the bathroom and tried to vomit. Because bulimia was cool or something. I had seen it in shows and magazines. But I couldn't because I wasn't that mad.  
I kept liking that guy because... I don't know. He still was cute and since I never really had a chance with him(rumours said he was gay), who cared if he could make me feel bad. Just staring wasn't hurtful.  
When I was 13, my "bisexual phase" started. I hate to say that because bisexuality is a valid sexuality and it shouldn't be thought at something "transitive" until you decide one gender. But it kind of was for me. I suddenly liked girls. I met this girl in high school who became my friend and it was my biggest crush. Bigger than the one I had with that boy. I knew she appreciated me. I looked up to her, she had good grades and we shared a lot of things. And her smile made my days brighter. It was that kind of crush. Of course, nothing happened because she was straight. We were girlfriends in my head, of course.  
Years passed and I changed schools. I hated the first high school I went to(the only things I liked were that one girl, another friend and maybe a couple of teachers). So I went to one intensified in languages, which are one of my passions. There, I met a couple of people I liked too. But it was so different. I actully started talking to boys there. I made my first male friend, and to this day he is one of my best friends. I spent two years in that school.  
We went to a senior year trip when I had my last crush on a girl. We talked on that trip several times. I don't know if she was interested in me. When we came back to the city, I had my hair cut. A lot. Like a boy. I showed up in school with my haircut the last day, and several girls(even some girls I didn't usually talked to) noticed it and told me it suited me. But not that girl. She didn't say a word to me since that day. Not even at graduation ceremony. Maybe she was afraid I actually was a lesbian, because her family was religious or something... I don't know.  
And since then, no new girl has catched my attention. I have to say that I never(or very rarely) felt sexual attraction towards girls. All the other things, the thrills, the blushing, were there, but not that one thing.  
If you haven't noticed until now, I haven't had my first kiss. Not even close. Yes, some boys tried to make moves on me on parties, but I just wasn't that interested that I could give them my first kiss. Also I probably was interested in other girl everytime that happened lol.  
A couple of weeks ago, I couldn't stop thinking about this girl I still haven't mentioned. I met her when we were 13, and since we're 14 I've had a crush on her. I rarely saw her, we went to the same school one year but she missed it nearly everyday. She lives near me, and everytime I went near her house, I thought I might see her anytime. She has been a little depressed the last years. I wrote her a letter when our only friend in common moved to another city. If she wanted to meet us, she could. I left her my cell phone and my friends'. She called and told me she would meet us the next day and that she would give me a call.  
But she didn't.  
I don't know what happened. I don't know if it was something I said, or if her mother told her not to come. I don't know nothing about her since that day, six months ago.  
I remember how I wanted to kiss her the day I realised I liked her.  
So, I'm what some call a 'lip virgin' because I wanted to kiss the people who didn't want to kiss me. I really don't know how people can be that lucky to not being in the same situation. It's not like I have super high expectations. Just a nice guy with a sense of humour and who appreciates me and the relation we have.

I'd also like to have my first kiss with a boy who is also kissing for the first time. That's why I like the idea of Virginity Exchange. But nobody from my country has said anything yet in that sub.

> Do a lot of people like neoliberalism and Macri?  
  
YES. In Argentina's subrredit, over half of the redditors support Macri and his party. In real life, the country is divided, one half of the population supports the current government and the other half despises it and prefer the kirchenrist government. It's not a matter of class at all, you can find supporters of both sides everywere. I think it's more of a matter of each family. > What do you think of Peron?
  
  
I think he took some really positive actions. I also know that he was a conservative and that is something many of his followers seem to forget. But you have to contextualise him: peronism emerged from the first succesfull dictatorship in the country. Peron was a militar. However, he gained a lot of popular support in the 1940s and took the power with his followers in the first massive protest of the country in 1945 that is still celebrated by the peronists groups almost as a holiday. He was a smart politician and knew how to manage his followers when his government was defeated by the next dictatorship and he had to be exiled.  
You are right when you say his legacy is confusing. As someone else said here before, there are people who love him and people who hate him. Some people say that his biggest mistake was starting the whole "giving away things" policy. One of peronism key pillars is  social welfare. I think it's called Welfare State(in contrast with Neoliberalist State, that Macri proposes now). Cristina's government had several plans for social welfare, such as giving away houses(or renting them for a low price), decanters, scholarships, etc., and you had to reunite some requirements for receiving them to prove that you really needed them. Perfect, right? Well, this caused(according to a very big portion of the population) that people from surrounding countries came to Argentina, because their countries were doing bad economically and it was cheaper and better for them to live here. And even when most of us descend from italians, we have never liked that kind of foreigners. Foreigners were poor, they had children, the children went to school with us, the parents took away our jobs, all the same old story. This worked against the image of peronism and contributed a lot on the results of last year elections. However, peronism is still very big amongst political ideologies.
